projects.name: Chasing606
projects.summary: An outdoor-inspired brand and its storefront, built so exploring the catalog feels as considered as the brand itself.
projects.lead: An outdoor-inspired brand from eastern Kentucky, and a storefront built so that exploring the catalog feels as considered as the brand itself.
notes: The first thing you see is the brand: a full-bleed photograph and one line, “From the heart of 606.” The shop comes second, once you know who you are buying from.
A shop in the brand’s own look
Product galleries, filtering and a cart sit inside the same design, so buying a shirt does not feel like leaving the site.
Their latest hunt, front and center
A film section puts the newest upload on the page, so the site feels alive and gives people a reason to come back.
projects.alt: The Chasing606 website scrolling from the hero, to the latest hunt video, to the footer

projects.name: Porter Property Maintenance
projects.summary: An established pressure-washing business, redesigned to be easier to understand and easier to contact.
projects.lead: A family-owned pressure-washing business in South Point, Ohio, redesigned so a homeowner can understand what they do and ask for an estimate in one tap.
notes: “Pressure washing, done right.” The logo, the town and two clear buttons answer who they are and what to do next before anyone scrolls.
Homeowners and businesses each get their own card with the exact services listed, so people find themselves quickly.
An estimate button sits in the header, mid-page and footer, so reaching out is always one tap away on a phone.

projects.name: Wonderfully Made
projects.summary: A faith-centered hair salon in Worthington, Kentucky, with a site that feels as warm as the chair: easy to book, and her real work front and center.
projects.lead: A faith-centered, vintage boho hair salon in Worthington, Kentucky, and a website that feels as warm as the chair: her own logo drawing itself on arrival, her real Facebook work on display, and booking as simple as a text.
notes: Her badge opens the site by drawing its own circle, writing out the name, then revealing the monogram. It is her artwork, just brought to life.
The salon already shares its color and blonding work on Facebook, so the portfolio shows those real posts instead of a second gallery she would have to keep up.
Booking that fits how she works
Pick your services and the site writes the text to Madison for you. No booking app to learn, and every request starts with a name and what the client wants.
